title_ar: هل يجوز جمع صوم السبت وأيام البيض والأيام الثلاثة والخميس و الإثنين بنية واحدة و في وقت واحد إذا أمكن الجمع بينها ؟
title_en: Is It Permissible to Combine the Fast of the Six Days, the White Days, the Three Days, Thursday and Monday under a Single Intention and at a Single Time, Where Combining Them Is Possible?
body_ar: السلام عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته شيخنا الفاضل السلام عليكم ورحمت الله وبركاته أحسن الله إليكم هل يجوز جمع صوم الست وأيام البيض والأيام الثلاثة والخميس و الإثنين بنية واحدة و في وقت واحد إذا أمكن الجمع بينها ؟ وما هو الأصل في جمع أكثر من نية في العمل الواحد هل هو الجواز أم المنع جزاكم الله خيرا وبارك فيكم الجواب : الذي يصوم أيام الليالي البيض و يكمل عليها بقية الستة يحصل له فضلان كالذي يصوم الاثنين و الخميس و لا يحتاج إلى نية مخصوصة غير نية الصوم و هذا الجمع في النية في النوافل أما الواجبات كالقضاء فيحصل لصاحبه فضل الأيام أيضا لكن لا يعد من الست لأنها زائدة على رمضان
body_en:
Peace be upon you, and the mercy of God and His blessings. Our excellent Sheikh, peace be upon you, and the mercy of God and His blessings. May God treat you well. Is it permissible to combine the fast of the six days, the white days, the three days, Thursday and Monday under a single intention and at a single time, where combining them is possible? And what is the baseline rule on combining more than one intention in a single act — is it permissibility or prohibition? May God reward you well and bless you.

Answer: One who fasts the days of the white nights and completes with them the remainder of the six obtains two merits, like one who fasts Monday and Thursday; and he needs no intention specific to that beyond the intention to fast. This combining is a combining in the intention within voluntary acts (nawāfil). As for the obligatory fasts, such as making up a missed fast, the one who performs them obtains the merit of those days as well, but it does not count as part of the six, because the six are additional to Ramadan.

flags.context: the title reads صوم السبت; the question in the body reads صوم الست, and the answer speaks of بقية الستة
options: the six days of Shawwal (reading الست, as the body and the answer have it)
the Saturday fast (reading السبت, as the title has it)
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT (house rule 11): title/body mismatch. The title says 'the fast of Saturday', the body of the question says 'the fast of the six', and the answer twice speaks of 'the remainder of the six', which can only be the six days of Shawwal. The title has almost certainly dropped a letter. The English title has been rendered on the body's reading, since the answer settles it, and the Arabic title is preserved unchanged. Flagged rather than corrected.

flags.arabic: ما هو الأصل في جمع أكثر من نية في العمل الواحد هل هو الجواز أم المنع
flags.context: the second half of the question, on the baseline rule for combining intentions
options: the question is not answered as a general rule
the sentence 'this combining is a combining in the intention within voluntary acts' is the answer to it, confined to the voluntary case
flags.note: The questioner asked a question of legal theory: is combining several intentions in one act permissible or barred as a general matter (tashrīk al-niyyah)? The Sheikh answers the particular cases and marks the distinction between voluntary and obligatory acts, but does not state the general rule the questioner asked for. Nothing has been supplied for it.

translator_notes: أيام الليالي البيض, literally 'the days of the white nights', are the thirteenth, fourteenth and fifteenth of the lunar month; 'the three days' in the question is the same practice. The Sheikh treats them as one item, which is why the answer has fewer elements than the question.
فضلان is rendered 'two merits' and not 'a double reward': the Arabic counts the two recommended fasts whose merit accrues, it does not quantify recompense.
